known_pitfall_claim: In the nonvertical case, membership of P'=(x_2,y_2) in M justifies substituting x_2=y_2/m at line 72.
pitfall_counterexample: Over ℚ, let m=2 and M={(x,y) | y=2x+1}. This is nonvertical with slope m. Take P'=(x₂,y₂)=(0,1). Then P'∈M because 1=2·0+1, but y₂/m=1/2≠0=x₂. Thus membership does not justify the substitution.
